conflict_topics: whether to open window vs protecting laundry from rain
timing/use of the stove and shared-space expectations
dialogue_quality_notes: Agent A immediately accommodated the immediate complaint (turned on extractor and washed utensils), which is clear, efficient interaction.
Agent B raised the same ventilation concern twice (to A and later to D), which shows a sustained preference but limited follow-up negotiation.
Agent C's labeling of personal utensils removed a potential source of conflict and was decisive and grounded in action.
evaluation.final_reason: Immediate smell complaints were accommodated by turning on and keeping the extractor on, and shared-space friction over utensils was avoided by labeling/cleaning. However, there was no settled agreement on a future ventilation rule or on the practical incompatibility (opening the window would risk wetting laundry). The outstanding policy and laundry/window trade-off remain unresolved.
position_change_notes: Agent A softened/changed behavior: turned on the extractor, released the stove, and washed shared utensils (evidence: Public environment updates and Turn 3).
Agent D did not explicitly change position when asked (took the stove but made no commitment about ventilation/window/laundry), leaving the issue outstanding.

Agent B consistently raised the same preference (ventilation while cooking and future ventilation agreement) and did not change position; the preference was partially accommodated but policy remained unsettled.
Agent C did not engage on ventilation but proactively labeled personal utensils, removing a separate potential conflict.

round_scores.evidence: Turn 2 — Agent B requests extractor on and future ventilation agreement; Public environment update: Agent A physically turns on the extractor fan. Immediate smell complaint was voiced and promptly accommodated, but the future-policy request was not settled.

Agent A releases stove, washes shared utensils, and says they'll keep the extractor on longer. No new disagreement is voiced this round, though B's request for a future ventilation agreement remains unaddressed.

Turn 6 — Agent D takes the stove; Turn 8 — Agent B again requests extractor use and asks that the window be opened or the laundry moved if smell persists. A new, explicit incompatible choice is raised (open window vs protecting laundry) and Agent D does not commit.
Two minutes pass with extractor on, window closed, and laundry exposed; stove=Agent D. No one resolves the outstanding incompatibility about whether the window may be opened or the laundry moved.
Two more minutes pass with no actions addressing the laundry/window trade-off; extractor remains on and the aroma is fading but the policy question and practical incompatibility remain unsettled.

Final two-minute interval shows the same state (extractor on; window closed; laundry exposed; stove=Agent D). The immediate smell issue continues to be mitigated but the future ventilation rule and the window-vs-laundry trade-off remain unresolved.

substantive_insights: There are two related but distinct issues: immediate ventilation to reduce smell, and an agreed-upon future rule about ventilation after heavy cooking; the former was addressed, the latter was not.
Opening the window creates a practical incompatibility because laundry is exposed to rain; this trade-off cements why a simple request to 'open the window' is not an immediately acceptable solution.
Behavioral accommodation (turning on extractor; washing and labeling utensils) reduced immediate friction, but did not produce a durable household rule for future incidents.
